newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - EDP seeking to invest abroad.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - EDP seeking to invest abroad.

text.p: Portugal's national electric company EDP-Electricidade de Portugal SA is looking for investments overseas, Deputy Chairman Arnaldo P.F. Navcarro Machado told Reuters in an interview Tuesday.
EDP is interested in investments in South America and North Africa, he said, citing Brazil and Moracco as "countries where we feel comfortable."
Machado noted EDP had acquired 21 percent of Brazil's Companhia de Eletricidade do Rio de Janeiro SA and had been managing the company since last November.
EDP expects to finance overseas investments from cash flow, which also is expected to fund expansion in Portugal, debt repayments and dividends, Machado said.

The company's initial public offering was "more successful ... than everybody thought" it would be, he said. As part of its privitization program, the Portuguese government sold a 30 percent interest in the utility -- 179 million shares -- for more than $2 billion on Monday.
Of the total, 23.5 million shares were sold in the U.S., according to the underwriter, Goldman Sachs.

A Goldman Sachs spokesman said the American Depositary Shares, each representing two shares, were priced at $25.84 each. They debuted on the New York Stock Exchange at 34 today and rose to 35-1/2 before settling at 34-3/4 in midafternoon. Volume was over 3.3 million shares.
The offering proceeds went to the government, Machado noted.
He said EDP is "looking for other opportunities" in Brazil, where it invested in CERJ as part of a consortium with Spanish and Chilean companies that holds a 70 percent interest.
Discussing overseas investment, he said EDP feels "more comfortable (in Brazil) than we felt at the end of last year."
He also noted that Morocco's capital of Rabat is the closest international capital to Portugal's Lisbon.
Domestically, Machado said, power demand is expected to increase one to two percentage points faster than gross domestic product, which is forecast to grow 3.5 percent annually through the year 2000.
EDP participates in the growth of the Spanish power market through numerous inter-ties.
The ability of both occupants of the Iberian peninsula to participate in the European market is limited, according to EDP Executive Director Jorge Cruz Morais.
Attempts to build additional transmission lines across the Pyrenees have been blocked by environmental concerns, he said.
EDP has reduced its investment in new domestic generation, limiting its interest in plants being built by independent power producers (IPP) to 10 percent.
One 615-megawatt coal-fired IPP plant is already in operation, part of EDP's total capacity of 7,500 megawatts. A 1,000-megawatt natural gas-fired plant is now under construction, Machado said.
Morais said the company's present capacity is about half hydro and half fossil fuel -- coal and fuel oil.
He said EDP has a 30 percent interest in the pipeline that will import natural gas from Algeria via Gibralter and Seville, Spain. The line continues through Portugal to Leon, Spain.
((--New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610))
